search_log: Searched "Plum Island" "Nelson DeMille" excerpt first chapter, author-site excerpts, and Google Books previews; located the author's complete Chapter One and an authorized Warner Books excerpt.
Searched "Plum Island" "first-person" narrator John Corey, point of view, and narrated by; located explicit whole-book descriptions identifying Corey as the first-person narrator.
Opened and inspected the Nelson DeMille Chapter One page, Bookreporter authorized excerpt, BookRags point-of-view analysis, and Michael Cavacini review before using them.

Searched "Plum Island" Nelson DeMille alternating point of view, multiple narrators, epistolary, and frame narrative; results produced no credible indication that this novel alternates person or contains a constitutive frame.
Google Books and library catalog results verified the work but supplied only metadata or synopsis-level material, so they were not used as person evidence.
person_note: The diagnostic quotes repeatedly expose John Corey participating as I/me across investigation, reflection, and action passages. Authorized sustained opening prose independently identifies Corey and preserves that voice, while whole-book sources describe the narration as exclusively first person. Third-person references merely describe other characters from Corey's perspective; dialogue and gnomic material are non-base. The feminine I in q00336 is necessarily local character speech and appears to be an upstream bucket issue, not an alternate narrator. No credible alternating, framed, or epistolary structure was found; the opening-only scope of the Tier A excerpts is mitigated by the distributed quote evidence and explicit whole-book descriptions.
